rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Wahy is anything used to indicate something to another, whether writing, gesture, or message.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : الوحي : كل شيء دللت به من كتاب أو إشارة أو رسالة

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Wahy is anything conveyed so that another knows it, however it is conveyed.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن فارس : كل ما ألقيته إلى غيرك حق يعلمه فهو : وحي ، كيف كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahy can also mean swift or sound; istawḥaynāhum means that we called them to cry out.
rows.anchor: والوحي : السريع . والوحي : الصوت . ويقال : استوحيناهم ، أي : استصرخناهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some define wahy as conveying an intended meaning to its recipient in the swiftest, gentlest way.
rows.anchor: وقد حد بعضهم الوحي فقال : إيصال المراد إلى الموحى إليه على أسرع وجه وألطفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahy can mean sending revelation.
rows.anchor: أحدها : الإرسال . ومنه قوله تعالى في النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahy can mean a gesture or sign.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الإشارة . ومنه قوله تعالى في مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahy can mean inspiration, including inspiration of the disciples, bee, and Moses’ mother.
rows.anchor: والثالث : الإلهام . ومنه قوله تعالى في المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahy can mean a command.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الأمر . ومنه قوله تعالى في الزلزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here wahy means speech.
rows.anchor: والخامس : القول . ومنه قوله تعالى في النجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahy can mean informing someone in a dream; Ibn Qutayba is named for this interpretation.
rows.anchor: والسادس : إعلام في المنام . ومنه قوله تعالى في عسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahy can mean informing by whispering, including Satan’s prompting and mutual embellishment of speech.
rows.anchor: والسابع : إعلام بالوسوسة . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ordinary Arabic, prostration is lowering the head even without touching the ground; every submissive person is called prostrating.
rows.anchor: السجود في اللغة : خفض الرأس وإن لم تصل الجبهة إلى الأرض . وكل ذليل فهو ساجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sujūd can mean ritual prostration, placing the forehead on the ground.
rows.anchor: أحدها : السجود الشرعي ، وهو وضع الجبهة على الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sujūd can mean ritual bowing.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الركوع الشرعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sujūd can mean compliance and submission.
rows.anchor: والثالث : الانقياد والاستسلام . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shajar is the plural of shajara and denotes any plant with a trunk.
rows.anchor: الشجر : جمع شجرة . وهي كل نبات له ساق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shajir, a valley, or land can describe a place abundant in trees.
rows.anchor: وواد شجير : كثير الشجر . وهذه الأرض أشجر من هذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb shajara can describe a dispute among people.
rows.anchor: وشجر بين القوم : إذا اختلف الأمر بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shajar can mean a tree with a trunk.
rows.anchor: أحدها : الشجر الذي له ساق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shajar can mean a grapevine; other views say the tree was a plant, a trunk, or wheat.
rows.anchor: الثاني : الكرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shajar can refer to an olive tree.
rows.anchor: الثالث : الزيتون . ومنه قوله تعالى في المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shajar can refer to the tree of Zaqqūm.
rows.anchor: الرابع : الزقوم . ومنه قوله تعالى في بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shajar can mean a palm tree.
rows.anchor: الخامس : النخلة . ومنه قوله تعالى في إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shajar can mean the colocynth tree.
rows.anchor: السادس : شجرة الحنظل . ومنه قوله تعالى في إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shajar can refer to an ʿawsaj tree.
rows.anchor: السابع : شجرة العوسج ( ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shajar can refer to a gourd plant.
rows.anchor: الثامن : شجرة القرع . ومنه قوله تعالى في الصافات

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: The green tree in the fire verse means marakh and ʿaffār wood used by Bedouins as fire sticks.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : أراد بها الزنود التي توري بها الأعراب من شجر المرخ والعفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tree beneath which allegiance was pledged was a samura tree.
rows.anchor: والعاشر : السمرة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadam is the familiar foot, from the ankle below the leg to the toes; it can also be metaphorical by context.
rows.anchor: القدم : العضو المعروف . وحده من مفصل الكعب تحت الساق إلى الأظفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadam can mean the bodily foot.
rows.anchor: أحدها : القدم المذكور . ومنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadam can mean prior choice or precedence.
rows.anchor: الثاني : سابقة الاختيار . ومنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Make our feet firm” means “make our hearts firm,” since feet stand firm through the heart.
rows.anchor: الثالث : القلب . ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadam can mean the self: a foot slipping after being firm means the self turning from obedience.
rows.anchor: الرابع : النفس . ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baṣīr is opposite of blind; baṣar can mean sight or knowledge, and baṣīr can mean knowledgeable.
rows.anchor: البصير : ضد الأعمى ، والبصر : واحد الأبصار . والبصر : أيضا العلم بالشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baṣīra can denote a rounded blood drop, a shield, or proof.
rows.anchor: والبصيرة : القطعة من الدم إذا وقعت على الأرض استدارت . والبصيرة : الترس . والبصيرة : البرهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbs baṣura and abṣara can mean knowing and seeing.
rows.anchor: يقال : بصرت بالشيء : إذا صرت بصيرا به عالما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the cited poem, baṣīr means a dog.
rows.anchor: والبصير : الكلب ، في قول القائل : - أرى نار ليلى أو يراني بصيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baṣīr can mean seeing with the heart.
rows.anchor: أحدها : البصير بالقلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baṣīr can mean seeing with the eye.
rows.anchor: والثاني : البصير بالعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baṣīr can mean insight into a proof.
rows.anchor: والثالث : البصير بالحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baṣīr can mean one who takes heed; the author’s teacher groups this under heart-sight.
rows.anchor: والرابع : المعتبر ، ومنه قوله تعالى في الذاريات

rows.speaker: شيخنا
rows.claim: The author’s teacher prefers to classify taking heed as heart-sight.
rows.anchor: وألحقه شيخنا بالقسم الأول وقال : هو من البصر بالقلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitna can mean misguidance.
rows.anchor: والثامن : الضلالة . ومنه قوله تعالى في المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitna can mean an excuse.
rows.anchor: والتاسع : المعذرة . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في الأنعام ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitna can mean a trial or object lesson for wrongdoers and unbelievers.
rows.anchor: والعاشر : العبرة . ومنه قوله تعالى في يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitna can mean madness.
rows.anchor: والحادي عشر : الجنون . ومنه قوله تعالى في نون والقلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitna can mean sin.
rows.anchor: والثاني عشر : الأثم . ومنه قوله تعالى في براءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitna can mean punishment.
rows.anchor: والثالث عشر : العقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitna can mean illness.
rows.anchor: والرابع عشر : المرض . ومنه قوله تعالى في براءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitna can mean decree.
rows.anchor: والخامس عشر : القضاء . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sāq is the familiar leg; a plant’s branch is also called its sāq.
rows.anchor: الأصل في الساق : العضو المعروف ، وكل نبات له غصن فغصنه ساقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sāq can mean the bodily leg; the cited al-Ṣād form as-sūq is its plural.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : العضو المعروف . ومنه قوله تعالى في ص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sāq can mean severity or hardship.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الشدة . ومنه قوله تعالى في نون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qibal can mean “at/with me,” and can also mean ability or capacity.
rows.anchor: بمعنى عند . يقال : ماله قبلي حق ، أي : عندي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qibal can mean capacity or ability.
rows.anchor: أحدها : الطاقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Pharaoh passage, min qablihi means “with him.”
rows.anchor: بمعنى ' مع ' . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحاقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qibal can mean a direction or side.
rows.anchor: والثالث : النحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qibalan can mean face-to-face or in plain view.
rows.anchor: والرابع : المعاينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qatl is an act leading to death; qitāl is the person or life struck, and fatal points are called maqātil.
rows.anchor: القتل : الفعل المؤدي إلى الموت . والقتال النفس . تقول قتلت فلانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Figuratively, killing something with knowledge means knowing it thoroughly; killing wine with water means mixing it.
rows.anchor: ويقال [ قتلت ] الشيء علما ، وقتلت الخمر بالماء : مزجتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qatl can mean enemy; the poem uses aqtaal for enemies.
rows.anchor: والقتل : العدو . وجمعه : أقتال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A girl’s taqattil can mean acting yielding toward a man until he falls in love.
rows.anchor: ويقال : تقتلت الجارية للرجل حتى عشقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A maqtal heart is one struck down by love, as in the verse cited from Imruʾ al-Qays.
rows.anchor: ويقال : قلب مقتل ، إذا قتله العشق . قال امرؤ القيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qatl can mean killing that causes death.
rows.anchor: أحدها : الفعل المميت للنفس

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: In the cited verse, faqtulūhum means “fight them,” according to Muqātil.
rows.anchor: أي : فقاتلوهم ) . قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qatl can be a curse or imprecation.
rows.anchor: والثالث : اللعن . ومنه قوله تعالى في الذاريات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qatl can mean torment or severe punishment.
rows.anchor: والرابع : التعذيب . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأحزاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qatl can mean knowledge or certainty.
rows.anchor: والخامس : العلم . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qatl can mean burying children alive.
rows.anchor: والسادس : الدفن للحي . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamīm means hot water; ḥamiyya is hot anger or jealousy, and ḥamīm can also mean a close relative.
rows.anchor: الحميم : الماء الحار . والحمية : حرارة الغضب والغيرة . ويقال : الحميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamīm can mean hot water.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : الماء الحار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamīm can mean a close blood relative.
rows.anchor: والثاني : القريب في النسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adhān is a call intended to inform the person being called of what is wanted.
rows.anchor: الأذان : نداء يقصد به إعلام المنادى بما يراد منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb adhina can mean listening attentively and responding; the earth listens to its Lord.
rows.anchor: فإذا أصغى إليه المنادى بالاستماع والاستجابة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said God listens to no one as He listens to a prophet reciting the Qur’an aloud.
rows.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' ما أذن الله لشيء ما أذن لنبي يتغنى بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adhān can mean calling or announcing to people.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : النداء . ( ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adhān can mean informing or making something known.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الإعلام ومنه قوله تعالى في براءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says calling and informing may be one sense, so the division is not sound.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يعد هذان الوجهان وجها واحدا ، فلا يصح التقسيم إذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idhn originally means release without restriction; “I gave ear to speech” means that I listened.
rows.anchor: الأصل في الإذن : الإطلاق من غير حجر . وأذنت للحديث استمعت

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet’s saying uses adhina in the sense of listening.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : ' ما أذن الله لشيء ما أذن لنبي يتغنى بالقرآن ' أي ما استمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idhn can mean permission itself, including permission for death or belief.
rows.anchor: أحدها : الإذن نفسه . ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idhn can mean a command.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الأمر . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idhn can mean will.
rows.anchor: والثالث : الإرادة . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qiyām is the human body’s upright posture; qawma is one standing, qiwām what something depends on, and qiwām can mean good stature.
rows.anchor: الأصل في القيام : انه انتصاب القامة من الآدمي وامتدادها إلى جهة العلو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qiyām can mean ordinary standing upright.
rows.anchor: أحدها : القيام المعروف الذي هو انتصاب القامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qiyām can mean security, or support for people’s affairs.
rows.anchor: الثاني : الأمن . ومنه قوله تعالى في المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqīmū al-ṣalāh means to perform or establish prayer.
rows.anchor: الثالث : الاتمام . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāʾim can mean maintaining justice over each soul.
rows.anchor: الرابع : العدل . ومنه قوله تعالى في الرعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qiyām can mean standing or being present.
rows.anchor: الخامس : الوقوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāma can mean rising to undertake a call or mission.
rows.anchor: السادس : النهوض بالدعوة . ومنه قوله تعالى في المدثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qiyām can mean coming to be or occurring, as in the Hour arising.
rows.anchor: السابع : الكون . ومنه قوله تعالى في مواضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāʾim can mean firm and standing, as in a settlement whose structure remains upright.
rows.anchor: الثامن : الثبوت . ومنه قوله تعالى في هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawwāmīn can mean people who speak repeatedly for justice.
rows.anchor: التاسع : القول . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāʾim can mean persistent or continually attending to something.
rows.anchor: العاشر : المواظبة . ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qiyām can mean livelihood or the support on which people’s living depends.
rows.anchor: الحادي عشر : القوام . ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lisān is the mouth’s organ and instrument of speech; lasin means skilled in speech, and lasan means eloquence.
rows.anchor: اللسان : العضو المعروف في الفم وهو آلة النطق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lisān can mean the tongue itself.
rows.anchor: أحدها : اللسان بعينه . ومنه قوله تعالى في الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lisān can mean a language.
rows.anchor: والثاني : اللغة . ومنه قوله تعالى في إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lisān can mean supplication or prayer.
rows.anchor: والثالث : الدعاء . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في المائدة ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lisān can mean good praise or favorable mention among later generations.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الثناء الحسن . ومنه قوله تعالى في الشعراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarya names a large gathering of people and derives from gathering; qaraʾtu al-māʾ means collecting water in a basin.
rows.anchor: القرية : اسم لما يجمع جماعة كثيرة من الناس . وهو اسم مأخوذ من الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basin holding collected water is called a maqrāh.
rows.anchor: ويقال : للحوض الذي فيه الماء : مقراة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says qarʾ means gathering and Qur’an is so named because its speech is collected.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : والقرء في اللغة الجمع . وسمي القرآن قرآنا لأنه كلام مجتمع

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the Qur’an is named for gathering and joining its sūras together.
rows.anchor: ( وقال ابن قتيبة : سمي القرآن قرآنا ) لأنه جمع السور وضمها

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda’s poem illustrates qaraʾa for carrying or gathering a fetus.
rows.anchor: وأنشد أبو عبيدة : - هجان اللون لم تقرأ جنينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 75:17, “its gathering and recitation” means its compilation.
rows.anchor: وقوله : ﴿ إن علينا جمعه وقرآنه ﴾ ، أي : تأليفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarya refers to Mecca in the cited passages.
rows.anchor: أحدها : مكة . ومنه قوله تعالى في النحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarya refers to Aylah, the settlement by the sea.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أيلة . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The village the Israelites were told to enter or inhabit is identified as Jericho.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أريحا . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The village in the passerby narrative is identified as Dayr Hirqal.
rows.anchor: الرابع : دير هرقل . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The town of the messengers in Yā Sīn is identified as Antioch.
rows.anchor: الخامس : أنطاكية . ومنه قوله تعالى في يس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The village in the punishment passage is identified as the village of Lot’s people.
rows.anchor: السادس : قرية قوم لوط . ومنه قوله تعالى في العنكبوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarya refers to Nineveh in the passage about its people believing.
rows.anchor: السابع : نينوى . ومنه قوله تعالى في يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarya refers to Egypt in the passage about asking the town where the brothers had been.
rows.anchor: الثامن : مصر . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma is a coordinating particle denoting sequence with delay; Amr comes after Zayd with an interval.
rows.anchor: ثم حرف مبني على الفتح وهو من حروف العطف ويفيد الترتيب والمهلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma retains its ordinary sense of sequence and interval in many passages.
rows.anchor: أحدها : بقاؤه على أصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma can function like wāw, “and”; the source applies this to 75:19.
rows.anchor: والثاني : بمعنى الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma can be redundant.
rows.anchor: والثالث : وقوعه زائدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samāʿ is perceiving sounds by hearing; samʿ is the faculty that perceives them.
rows.anchor: السماع : إدراك السمع المسموعات . والسمع : الحاسة المدركة للأصوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra on sīn, samʿ can mean good renown; it can also denote the offspring of a wolf and hyena.
rows.anchor: والسمع : بكسر السين ، الذكر الجميل ، والسمع أيضا : ولد ( الذئب من الضبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samāʿ with fatḥa on sīn and kasra on ʿayn can be an imperative meaning “listen.”
rows.anchor: ويقال : سماع بفتح السين وكسر العين بمعنى : أسمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samāʿ can mean ordinary auditory perception; this is the general sense.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : إدراك السمع المسموعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samāʿ can mean the heart’s hearing, or accepting what is heard.
rows.anchor: والثاني : سماع القلب وهو قبوله للمسموع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-aʿmā can mean a person blind in sight.
rows.anchor: والثاني : الأعمى البصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-aʿmā can mean blind to proof or evidence.
rows.anchor: والثالث : الأعمى عن الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-aʿmā can stand for a disbeliever.
rows.anchor: والرابع : الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā can function as a negative particle.
rows.anchor: والثاني : بمعنى النفي . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā can express exclamation, with an implied sense of “what” or “how.”
rows.anchor: والثالث : بمعنى التعجب وتقديره أي شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā can be a relative pronoun meaning “that which.”
rows.anchor: والرابع : بمعنى ' الذي ' . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في البقرة ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā can mean “as”; some group this with the relative-pronoun sense.
rows.anchor: والخامس : بمعنى ' كما '

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā can be an interrogative particle.
rows.anchor: والسادس : بمعنى الاستفهام . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā can mean “who” or “the one that” in oaths; some group it with the relative sense.
rows.anchor: والسابع : بمعنى ' من ' . ومنه قوله تعالى في الشمس

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba reports Abū ʿAmr’s view that mā in the oaths means “that which.”
rows.anchor: فذكر ابن قتيبة : عن أبي عمرو أنه قال : هي بمعنى

rows.speaker: أهل مكة
rows.claim: Meccans say on hearing thunder, “Glory to the One whom it glorifies,” illustrating mā as a relative form.
rows.anchor: وأهل مكة يقولون إذا سمعوا الرعد : سبحان ما سبحت له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nisyān with kasra nūn and sukūn sīn is distinguished from the form with both vowels open, called the twin of the sciatic nerve.
rows.anchor: النسيان : مكسور النون ، مسكن السين

rows.speaker: من لم يهمز
rows.claim: The form nunsihā in 2:106 is cited on the reading of those who do not hamza.
rows.anchor: على قراءة من لم يهمز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nisyān can mean deliberate abandonment.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : الترك مع العمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nisyān can mean the opposite of remembering.
rows.anchor: والثاني : خلاف الذكر
